_format: One rule per stale or risky three.js API. pattern is a JavaScript regex source (flag g added by tw lint). since = the release that deprecated it (or removed it when there was no deprecation period); removed = the release that deleted it. status: removed | deprecated | pitfall. Severity is derived: error once the project's release is at or past `removed`, warn when deprecated, the rule's own severity for pitfalls. requires = a regex the file must match before the rule applies (for names that are only stale in a three.js context). sample must match the pattern and ok must not; tw kb validate checks both. verify = true means the release number still needs a primary-source check.

rules.message: since r155 WebGLRenderer applies toneMapping and outputColorSpace only when it renders straight to the screen; with three.js's own EffectComposer (three/addons/postprocessing/) in the way, the final image is linear and untonemapped unless an OutputPass runs last (the unrelated pmndrs "postprocessing" npm package has a different EffectComposer and is not this rule's target)
rules.fix: composer.addPass(new OutputPass()) as the last pass
rules.sample: import { EffectComposer } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js'; const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer, target); composer.addPass(new RenderPass(scene, camera));
rules.ok: import { EffectComposer } from 'three/addons/postprocessing/EffectComposer.js'; const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer, target); composer.addPass(new RenderPass(scene, camera)); composer.addPass(new OutputPass());
rules.source: three.js manual, EffectComposer / OutputPass pages; behaviour change verified against three 0.186.1's src/renderers/webgl/WebGLRenderer.js (render-to-screen check) and examples/jsm/postprocessing/OutputPass.js

rules.message: this typed BufferAttribute was given an array that is written again later, but the typed subclasses copy the array they are given (new Float32Array(array)), so those writes never reach the GPU, silently

rules.source: three.js src/core/BufferAttribute.js: Float32BufferAttribute's constructor calls super(new Float32Array(array), ...); markdavidrogers-web PR #37 lost a whole road this way (LEARNINGS L-20261004-1)
